changes.headline: Blockade enforcement hardens from both sides; second Saturday tanker strike
changes.dek: US disabled M/V Ocean Molica (Gulf of Oman, Sat) for running the Iran blockade; UKMTO logged an outbound tanker struck at 19:20 UTC Oct 10 in the Strait (fire onboard, crew safe); coalition claims 136 Houthi targets destroyed Saturday.. Saturday was the blockade chapter. CENTCOM says a US fighter jet disabled the propulsion of the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also reported as Arika Sun) in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored repeated warnings and tried to break the US naval blockade of Iranian ports; no crew casualties. The IRGC, meanwhile, says it struck a supertanker in the Strait on an unauthorized route and warned of 'horrific fire' for ships ignoring its rules. UKMTO logged two tanker strikes Saturday: 08:00 UTC NW of Oman (bridge damaged, crew safe) and 19:20 UTC in the Strait (fire onboard, crew safe; later shipping press reported minor structural damage near Khasab with the vessel continuing - reporting still settling). The coalition spokesman claimed 136 Houthi targets destroyed Saturday as ground fighting raged around Taiz; fresh Saudi airstrikes hit Hajjah and a fuel station in Hodeidah.
changes.balance_read: The war premium has two-way risk. The Hormuz incident rate is accelerating, not slowing - a premium-carrying market with catch-up fuel if escalation surprises, and a flush risk concentrated on any real de-escalation (Strait reopening, US-Iran deal). Friday night's US retaliatory strikes have already overtaken Trump's no-strike-before-midterms pledge. Two competing blockades are now being shot at commercial shipping; that is the structural leg of the bid, not the storm.
changes.publishers: DeepDraft SITREP, Oct 11, 2026; UKMTO advisories via Defcon/Ship&Bunker/Assafina, Oct 10-11, 2026; coalition spokesman via wire, Oct 10, 2026; al-Masirah via IANS/Xinhua, Oct 10, 2026

changes.headline: Isaias storm story over; restart watch begins
changes.dek: Landfall near Destin, FL late Friday at ~105 mph (wire), post-tropical; Pascagoula and Saraland spared; ~830k without power; NHC 08:00 UTC Oct 11: no active Gulf tropical threat.. Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida late Friday at about 105 mph per wire reports, weakened to a post-tropical cyclone, and the track spared the Texas/Louisiana refinery clusters and the major Mississippi/Alabama plants - Chevron Pascagoula (356 kb/d) and Vertex Saraland are the plants in the track zone. About 830,000 customers are without power across Florida, Alabama, and Georgia, and power restoration gates the restart of offshore production: BSEE Friday had ~71.5% of Gulf oil shut in (~1.5 Mb/d), 58.8% of gas, 129 of 371 platforms evacuated. Cumulative production loss ~9 Mbbl (Earth Science Associates). NHC's 08:00 UTC Oct 11 advisory: no active Gulf tropical threat (Isaias post-tropical; other systems active elsewhere only).
changes.balance_read: The storm bid unwinds as ~1.5 Mb/d comes back over days, barring damage; the Thursday-Friday rally was never the storm alone (Iran drones, thin Hormuz transits, and Friday's US retaliatory strikes were the structural legs). BSEE Monday is the next physical number that matters; restarts gated on power restoration could stretch the timeline.
changes.publishers: Wire reports, Oct 10-11, 2026; NHC 08:00 UTC Oct 11, 2026; BSEE via AP wire, Oct 9, 2026; Earth Science Associates

changes.headline: Diesel deal paper: licenses, not loadings
changes.dek: GL-135 names no volumes, buyers, or counterparties; does not repeal the 2022 statutory ban; Moscow's export ban runs through October; Kyiv will keep striking refineries (FT).. The diesel deal now exists on paper as three documents, none of which names a buyer. OFAC General License 135 (signed Oct 9, 14:43 EDT) authorizes Russian-origin diesel transactions through 12:01 a.m. EDT April 7, 2027 - no volumes, no counterparties, one exclusion on Russian sovereign bank accounts. The Kremlin readout confirms willingness to supply, no tonnage, no dates. The tonnage (300k Oct / 500k Nov / 1M Dec, possibly ~3 Mt/month) comes from Deputy PM Novak. The legal caveat: analysts note GL-135 does not expressly repeal the 2022 statutory import ban enacted by Congress - the license covers the OFAC sanctions regulations only, and members of Congress are already objecting. Delivery caveats: Russia's own diesel export ban runs through October (in place since July 8); a senior Ukrainian official told the FT Kyiv will continue striking Russian refineries despite the deal; EU/UK sanctions unchanged. Diesel futures fell 4.6% Friday post-settle. Against the bearish inputs: US diesel $6.23/gal and record-seasonal-low stocks since 1982.
changes.balance_read: The $100+ crack regime (Friday close $107.16, fifth straight day; 3-2-1 at $62.78) faces its biggest fundamental threat, but the threat is still announcements, not loadings. Until a Russian cargo actually moves, record-low stocks reassert. The regime is a two-way trade now.
changes.publishers: OFAC General License 135, Oct 9, 2026; TASS (Novak); FT (Ukraine official); Diplomacy and Law / Greengale analysis, Oct 10-11, 2026; Ship & Bunker, Oct 9-10, 2026

changes.headline: WCS front holds; December seasonal wide; freight the live driver
changes.dek: ICE Oct 9: TMW Nov26 -$24.78, Dec26 -$25.60 (widest); ARV-TMW Nov +$8.74; CalRock Oct 9 physical Nov26 -$25.55 (77c wider than screen).. No new settles over the weekend; the Oct 9 marks carry. ICE: TMW Nov26 -$24.78, Dec26 -$25.60 (still the widest tenor), Jan27 -$24.30, Feb27 -$22.45; ARV Nov26 -$16.04; ARV-TMW November +$8.74, the implied Hardisty-to-Houston export arb, still healthy. CalRock Oct 9 (personal): physical WCS Hardisty Nov26 -$25.55, 77 cents wider than the thin ICE front; Dec26 -$25.60, an exact match; physical Nov26 traded -25.25 to -25.55 on 210,000 m3 Friday - real liquidity, with the screen flattering November. The freight read: the Joliet restart did not rebound the diff, so the outage was not the driver. TD3C at WS 1058 (Gibson, Oct 1) vs 677 early September; TD9 at WS 681 (Baltic, Oct 2) vs ~324 a month ago - the TMX-to-Asia arb is uneconomic and barrels that cannot clear east price down to clear at a long USGC. The November Mainline apportionment notice (~Oct 19) is the decision point for the binding-from-November base case.
changes.balance_read: Arb-clearing dynamics, not refinery outages, explain the persistent WCS weakness: freight traps barrels and the clearing mechanism is price. December is already pricing the seasonal wide; the ~Oct 19 apportionment notice arbitrates whether the binding-from-November base case holds.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 9, 2026; CalRock EOD (personal), Oct 9, 2026; Gibson weekly, Oct 1, 2026; Baltic Exchange weekly via thedcn, Oct 2, 2026

changes.headline: Bank base cases split $30 wide
changes.dek: Reuters Oct 11: JPM Brent $58/$57; Goldman $85 Dec 26/$80 27; BofA YE26 $95, 27 $80, tail >$150; StanChart $92/$89.50; UBS $120+ if attacks renew.. Reuters' Oct 11 forecast roundup shows the street admitting it does not know which regime it is in: JPMorgan at $58 (2026) / $57 (2027) on oversupply; Goldman raised to $85 (Dec 2026) / $80 (2027) with an adverse case above $120; BofA year-end 2026 $95 (from $83), 2027 ~$80, tail 'well above $150' if disruption runs into spring 2027; Standard Chartered $92 / $89.50; UBS raised, $120+ if attacks renew. The 2027 spread between JPM and StanChart is over $30. Dubai spot fell $2.20 to $108.50 on Oct 9 (KNOC via Aju Press) even as Brent rose - the Middle East marker softening against the futures bid. Curve shape: steep backwardation on both legs - tight now, glut later.
changes.balance_read: The forecast fan is the honest position: oversupply base cases and supply-shock tails coexist, and the market is pricing both. Let the curve shape (backwardation = tight-now) do the talking instead of a single-cause narrative.
changes.publishers: Reuters via Discovery Alert / Aju Press, Oct 11, 2026

changes.headline: SPR exchange award pending; positioning light on WTI
changes.dek: No DOE award announcement as of early Sunday; COT as-of Oct 6: WTI MM net +53,598 (29th percentile); Brent MM net +201,052.. The SPR 40 Mbbl exchange award is still pending - bids were due Oct 6 (11:00 CT), no DOE announcement. The award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery and is the next real data point for Gulf sour pricing (SPR at ~284 Mbbl, lowest since 1982). Positioning (COT as-of Oct 6, released Oct 9; no new vintage until Friday): WTI managed-money net +53,598, 29th percentile of the 1-year range - the long overhang is largely gone; Brent managed-money net +201,052, still long-heavy against ~110k of shorts. Specs went into the Oct 8-9 rally light on WTI: a bearish headline has little left to flush there, while Brent's flush risk sits on a de-escalation headline.
changes.balance_read: Thin WTI length means an escalation shock has catch-up fuel; Brent's 201k of net length is the de-escalation flush risk. The SPR award, when it lands, is the next physical pricing event for Gulf sour.
changes.publishers: energy.gov; Reuters; CFTC/ICE COT, as-of Oct 6, released Oct 9, 2026
